Continue the GuideMate capstone (MVP #1: name→Nav2 navigation, sim-only, lidar-only).
Read my memory first (MEMORY.md + the guidemate-* notes) — it has full context.

Where we are: build-order steps 1–3 are DONE. The maze map is finished and
validated — but NOT via SLAM. We generated it directly from the world SDF
(ground-truth geometry) with ~/robotics/sdf_to_map.py → ~/robotics/maps/maze_truth.
{pgm,yaml}: complete, exact, in the WORLD frame. Validated with ~/robotics/
scan_check.py (live lidar transformed to world) → 98% of returns land on map walls.

Key environment facts (in memory, don't re-derive): the sim MUST run in software
rendering — GPU/d3d12 breaks the lidar (all range_min). RTF is ~0.02 (slow, that's
accepted). After any sim relaunch, sim-time resets to 0, so RESTART any use_sim_time
node (SLAM/AMCL) or it freezes. Robot spawns at world (0,0); drive via
/robot_1/cmd_vel_unstamped; ground-truth pose on /robot_1/sim_ground_truth_pose.

Start the sim yourself in a dedicated terminal before we begin (so it persists):
  bash ~/robotics/sim_start_headless.sh

Now let's do the next milestone: bring up Nav2 + AMCL localization against
maze_truth and send one test goal — this proves the map is nav-ready end-to-end
in the world frame. Then step 4: define a few named destinations by picking (x,y,θ)
straight off the map in world coords. Then step 6: the name→pose→Nav2-goal core node
+ trivial dispatcher + CLI adapter. Work with me interactively, and step back to
high-level/environment differences before drilling into details.

That carries all the hard-won context (software-only rendering, sim-time-reset gotcha, the validated world-frame map, the tools) and points straight at the next milestone. See you in the next step.

2	name: guidemate-sim-gpu-rendering-fix
3	description: GuideMate WSL render dilemma — GPU (d3d12) is fast but BREAKS sensors (lidar all range_min); software renders sensors correctly but slow. Must use software + strip sensors for speed.
4	metadata:
5	  node_type: memory
6	  type: project
7	  originSessionId: eaf3798d-dd5e-460b-98ce-6a9551e35967
8	---
9	
10	**HEADLINE (2026-07-05): On this WSL box, GPU GL rendering BREAKS Gazebo sensors — CONFIRMED on BOTH GPUs. Software/CPU rendering (`LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1`) is the ONLY viable mode. Do NOT re-open the GPU path.** Re-tested this session (empirical lidar check, world=maze): NVIDIA RTX 3050 d3d12 → all 640 beams = range_min (0.164) broken; **AMD iGPU d3d12 → identical, all beams range_min broken** (verified NVIDIA at 0% util so AMD really rendered). The culprit is the **d3d12 Mesa backend (DirectX-12 GL translation), NOT the GPU** — swapping cards can't fix it. Why no other GPU path exists here: WSL ships NO native NVIDIA GL/Vulkan ICD (only libnvidia encode/ml/opticalflow + CUDA); the only registered hardware-capable Vulkan route is Mesa `dzn` = Vulkan-on-D3D12, which re-enters the same broken D3D12 layer. So zink-on-GPU would inherit the same bug; zink-on-lavapipe is just software. `sim_start.sh` DEFAULT is `RENDER=gpu` (BROKEN) — always launch via `sim_start_headless.sh` (forces software) or `RENDER=software`. Note: `.bashrc` already exports `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` as the login default. Both GPUs also hang the GUI black on first launch; server sometimes comes up on 2nd try but lidar stays dead.
11	
12	The render backends, tested (world=maze):
13	- **d3d12 GPU** (RTX 3050 or AMD iGPU via WSLg): sim runs fast (RTF ~0.067, 4.6x) BUT **all 640 lidar beams read range_min (0.164) = garbage**. GPU renders the GUI fine but offscreen sensor depth readback is broken. Useless for SLAM/nav.
14	- **zink** (GL-on-Vulkan): Gazebo can't create a GL context at all — `glx: failed to create drisw screen`, OGRE `Unable to create glx context`, Qt aborts, gazebo process dies. Non-viable.
15	- **software (llvmpipe)**: valid lidar (ranges 1.0-11.6m, 639/640 valid) BUT slow (RTF ~0.015 with GUI + all sensors). THE ONLY MODE WITH WORKING SENSORS.
16	
17	Why: Gazebo renders sensors through OGRE's GLX path (`Sensors.cc → Loading plugin [gz-rendering-ogre]`), same context type as the GUI. The WSL GPU GL drivers mishandle offscreen render-to-texture depth.
18	
19	**CORRECTION (2026-07-05, Shibo): the "RTF 0.02 → 0.634 = 32x" claim below is FALSE.** Under software rendering the RTF stays ~0.02 even WITH the physics-timestep change and the create3 cliff/IR sensor rate cuts. Those levers did not deliver the claimed 32x. Treat software RTF as ~0.02 (slow); robot-SPEED remains the only useful runtime lever. Original (overstated) notes kept below for the config details only:
20	
21	**Speed levers tried under software (RTF gains were NOT as large as first claimed — see correction above):** two levers, applied together:
22	1. **Physics timestep** — `maze.sdf` (`irobot_create_gz_bringup/worlds/maze.sdf`) `max_step_size` 0.001→0.004, `real_time_update_rate` 1000→250. 4x less physics work; fine for a flat diffdrive robot. This was a big part of the win.
23	2. **Sensor render-rate flood** — the killer was ~11 create3 ray sensors (4 cliff + 7 IR) each rendering at **62 Hz** = ~680 render passes/sec on the CPU. Dropped to 2 Hz in `irobot_create_description/urdf/sensors/{cliff_sensor,ir_intensity,ir_opcode_receivers}.urdf.xacro` (the `update_rate` prop/param). NOTE: stripping the OAK-D camera barely helped (only 30 passes/sec) — the 62 Hz ray-sensor count was the real flood.
24	Also done earlier: camera sensor commented out in `turtlebot4_description/urdf/sensors/oakd.urdf.xacro`; rplidar 62→10 Hz in `rplidar.urdf.xacro`; headless (`sim_start_headless.sh` + `sim_headless.launch.py`, server-only `gz sim -s`) — headless alone barely helped in software (GUI wasn't the cost). All edited vendor files have `.stock.bak` backups (chown'd to user). **Whenever the sim is relaunched, sim time resets to 0 — RESTART slam_toolbox (and any use_sim_time node), else it freezes rejecting "past" timestamps.** Final viable config: `RENDER=software` + headless + physics 4ms/250 + create3 sensors 2 Hz → RTF ~0.63, valid lidar.
25	
26	Also fixed this session: `sim_start.sh` had `set -u` which crashed on ROS `setup.bash` (unbound AMENT_TRACE_SETUP_FILES) — wrapped in `set +u`/`set -u`. `mesa-utils` installed (glxinfo). Clock knob useless below RTF 1.0; robot-SPEED is the only useful runtime speed lever. See [[guidemate-sim-facts]], [[guidemate-mvp-plan]], [[debugging-step-back-over-detail-drilling]].
27

Why no other GPU path exists here: WSL ships NO native NVIDIA GL/Vulkan ICD (only libnvidia encode/ml/opticalflow + CUDA); the only registered hardware-capable Vulkan route is Mesa `dzn` = Vulkan-on-D3D12, which re-enters the same broken D3D12 layer. So zink-on-GPU would inherit the same bug; zink-on-lavapipe is just software. `sim_start.sh` DEFAULT is `RENDER=gpu` (BROKEN) — always launch via `sim_start_headless.sh` (forces software) or `RENDER=software`. Note: `.bashrc` already exports `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` as the login default. Both GPUs also hang the GUI black on first launch; server sometimes comes up on 2nd try but lidar stays dead.

The render backends, tested (world=maze):
- **d3d12 GPU** (RTX 3050 or AMD iGPU via WSLg): sim runs fast (RTF ~0.067, 4.6x) BUT **all 640 lidar beams read range_min (0.164) = garbage**. GPU renders the GUI fine but offscreen sensor depth readback is broken. Useless for SLAM/nav.
- **zink** (GL-on-Vulkan): Gazebo can't create a GL context at all — `glx: failed to create drisw screen`, OGRE `Unable to create glx context`, Qt aborts, gazebo process dies. Non-viable.
- **software (llvmpipe)**: valid lidar (ranges 1.0-11.6m, 639/640 valid) BUT slow (RTF ~0.015 with GUI + all sensors). THE ONLY MODE WITH WORKING SENSORS.

Why: Gazebo renders sensors through OGRE's GLX path (`Sensors.cc → Loading plugin [gz-rendering-ogre]`), same context type as the GUI. The WSL GPU GL drivers mishandle offscreen render-to-texture depth.

**CORRECTION (2026-07-05, Shibo): the "RTF 0.02 → 0.634 = 32x" claim below is FALSE.** Under software rendering the RTF stays ~0.02 even WITH the physics-timestep change and the create3 cliff/IR sensor rate cuts. Those levers did not deliver the claimed 32x. Treat software RTF as ~0.02 (slow); robot-SPEED remains the only useful runtime lever. Original (overstated) notes kept below for the config details only:

**Speed levers tried under software (RTF gains were NOT as large as first claimed — see correction above):** two levers, applied together:
1. **Physics timestep** — `maze.sdf` (`irobot_create_gz_bringup/worlds/maze.sdf`) `max_step_size` 0.001→0.004, `real_time_update_rate` 1000→250. 4x less physics work; fine for a flat diffdrive robot. This was a big part of the win.
2. **Sensor render-rate flood** — the killer was ~11 create3 ray sensors (4 cliff + 7 IR) each rendering at **62 Hz** = ~680 render passes/sec on the CPU. Dropped to 2 Hz in `irobot_create_description/urdf/sensors/{cliff_sensor,ir_intensity,ir_opcode_receivers}.urdf.xacro` (the `update_rate` prop/param). NOTE: stripping the OAK-D camera barely helped (only 30 passes/sec) — the 62 Hz ray-sensor count was the real flood.
Also done earlier: camera sensor commented out in `turtlebot4_description/urdf/sensors/oakd.urdf.xacro`; rplidar 62→10 Hz in `rplidar.urdf.xacro`; headless (`sim_start_headless.sh` + `sim_headless.launch.py`, server-only `gz sim -s`) — headless alone barely helped in software (GUI wasn't the cost). #!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Validate the ground-truth map against live lidar, in the WORLD frame.

Stationary at spawn: the RPLIDAR is 360deg, so one scan sees all directions.
Collect a few scans, transform every beam endpoint to world coords via the
ground-truth pose, and overlay them (red) on the truth map. Red points should
sit exactly on the black walls. Red sticking PAST a wall => that wall is too
short/missing in the map (Shibo's west-wall question).

Run after: bash ~/robotics/sim_start_headless.sh   (no SLAM needed)
"""
import math, numpy as np, yaml
import rclpy
from rclpy.node import Node
from rclpy.qos import qos_profile_sensor_data
from sensor_msgs.msg import LaserScan
from nav_msgs.msg import Odometry
from PIL import Image

BASE = '/home/baishibo123/robotics/maps/maze_truth'
y = yaml.safe_load(open(BASE + '.yaml'))
res = y['resolution']; ox, oy = y['origin'][0], y['origin'][1]
gray = np.array(Image.open(BASE + '.pgm').convert('L'))
H, W = gray.shape

rclpy.init(); n = Node('scan_check'); buf = {'scans': []}
def on_scan(m): buf['scans'].append((m, buf.get('pose')))
def on_pose(m): buf['pose'] = m.pose.pose
n.create_subscription(LaserScan, '/robot_1/scan', on_scan, qos_profile_sensor_data)
n.create_subscription(Odometry, '/robot_1/sim_ground_truth_pose', on_pose, qos_profile_sensor_data)

# collect ~15 scans
n_wait = 0
while len([s for s in buf['scans'] if s[1] is not None]) < 15 and n_wait < 200:
    rclpy.spin_once(n, timeout_sec=0.1); n_wait += 1

scans = [s for s in buf['scans'] if s[1] is not None]
print(f'collected {len(scans)} scans with pose')
if not scans:
    print('NO scan+pose — is the sim up (software headless)?'); rclpy.shutdown(); exit()

rgb = np.stack([gray, gray, gray], axis=-1)
hit = tot = 0
p0 = scans[-1][1]
print(f'robot world pose x={p0.position.x:.2f} y={p0.position.y:.2f}')
# base_link -> lidar static TF (from tf2_echo): offset + 90deg yaw mount
LID_DX, LID_DY, LID_YAW = -0.04, 0.0, math.pi/2
for s, p in scans:
    q = p.orientation
    yaw = math.atan2(2*(q.w*q.z+q.x*q.y), 1-2*(q.y*q.y+q.z*q.z))
    # lidar origin in world = base pose + rotated mount offset
    px = p.position.x + LID_DX*math.cos(yaw) - LID_DY*math.sin(yaw)
    py = p.position.y + LID_DX*math.sin(yaw) + LID_DY*math.cos(yaw)
    for i, r in enumerate(s.ranges):
        if not math.isfinite(r) or r <= s.range_min or r >= s.range_max:
            continue
        a = yaw + LID_YAW + s.angle_min + i*s.angle_increment   # + lidar mount yaw
        wx = px + r*math.cos(a); wy = py + r*math.sin(a)
        c = int((wx-ox)/res); row = int(H-(wy-oy)/res)
        if 0 <= row < H and 0 <= c < W:
            tot += 1
            rgb[row, c] = [255, 0, 0]                    # scan return = red
            if (gray[max(0,row-2):row+3, max(0,c-2):c+3] < 50).any():
                hit += 1
# mark robot pose green
rc = int((p0.position.x-ox)/res); rr = int(H-(p0.position.y-oy)/res)
if 0 <= rr < H and 0 <= rc < W:

import os
from pathlib import Path

from ament_index_python.packages import get_package_share_directory
from launch import LaunchDescription
from launch.actions import DeclareLaunchArgument, IncludeLaunchDescription, SetEnvironmentVariable
from launch.launch_description_sources import PythonLaunchDescriptionSource
from launch.substitutions import LaunchConfiguration, PathJoinSubstitution
from launch_ros.actions import Node


ARGUMENTS = [
    DeclareLaunchArgument('namespace', default_value='robot_1',
                          description='Robot namespace'),
    DeclareLaunchArgument('rviz', default_value='false',
                          choices=['true', 'false'], description='Start rviz.'),
    DeclareLaunchArgument('world', default_value='maze',
                          description='Simulation World'),
    DeclareLaunchArgument('model', default_value='standard',
                          choices=['standard', 'lite'],
                          description='Turtlebot4 Model'),
]
for pose_element in ['x', 'y', 'z', 'yaw']:
    ARGUMENTS.append(DeclareLaunchArgument(pose_element, default_value='0.0',
                     description=f'{pose_element} component of the robot pose.'))


def generate_launch_description():
    pkg_turtlebot4_gz_bringup = get_package_share_directory('turtlebot4_gz_bringup')
    pkg_irobot_create_gz_bringup = get_package_share_directory('irobot_create_gz_bringup')
    pkg_turtlebot4_description = get_package_share_directory('turtlebot4_description')
    pkg_irobot_create_description = get_package_share_directory('irobot_create_description')
    pkg_ros_gz_sim = get_package_share_directory('ros_gz_sim')

    gz_resource_path = SetEnvironmentVariable(
        name='GZ_SIM_RESOURCE_PATH',
        value=':'.join([
            os.path.join(pkg_turtlebot4_gz_bringup, 'worlds'),
            os.path.join(pkg_irobot_create_gz_bringup, 'worlds'),
            str(Path(pkg_turtlebot4_description).parent.resolve()),
            str(Path(pkg_irobot_create_description).parent.resolve())
        ])
    )

    gz_sim_launch = PathJoinSubstitution([pkg_ros_gz_sim, 'launch', 'gz_sim.launch.py'])

    # Headless Gazebo: -s = server only (no GUI), -r = run on start.
    gazebo = IncludeLaunchDescription(
        PythonLaunchDescriptionSource([gz_sim_launch]),
        launch_arguments=[
            ('gz_args', [LaunchConfiguration('world'), '.sdf', ' -s', ' -r', ' -v 1'])
        ]
    )

    clock_bridge = Node(
        package='ros_gz_bridge', executable='parameter_bridge', name='clock_bridge',
        output='screen',
        arguments=['/clock' + '@rosgraph_msgs/msg/Clock' + '[gz.msgs.Clock'])

    robot_spawn = IncludeLaunchDescription(
        PythonLaunchDescriptionSource([PathJoinSubstitution(
            [pkg_turtlebot4_gz_bringup, 'launch', 'turtlebot4_spawn.launch.py'])]),
        launch_arguments=[
            ('namespace', LaunchConfiguration('namespace')),
            ('rviz', LaunchConfiguration('rviz')),
            ('x', LaunchConfiguration('x')),
            ('y', LaunchConfiguration('y')),
            ('z', LaunchConfiguration('z')),
            ('yaw', LaunchConfiguration('yaw'))]
    )

    ld = LaunchDescription(ARGUMENTS)
    ld.add_action(gz_resource_path)
    ld.add_action(gazebo)
    ld.add_action(clock_bridge)
    ld.add_action(robot_spawn)
    return ld

# Run in a DEDICATED terminal:  bash ~/robotics/sim_start_headless.sh [world]

WORLD="${1:-maze}"

set +u
source /opt/ros/jazzy/setup.bash
set -u
unset ROS_DISCOVERY_SERVER ROS_SUPER_CLIENT FASTRTPS_DEFAULT_PROFILES_FILE \
      ROS_AUTOMATIC_DISCOVERY_RANGE FASTDDS_BUILTIN_TRANSPORTS
export ROS_DOMAIN_ID=0
# SOFTWARE rendering is MANDATORY: GPU (d3d12) breaks Gazebo sensors (lidar all range_min).
# See guidemate-sim-gpu-rendering-fix memory. Speed is reclaimed by headless + fewer sensors.
export LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1
unset GALLIUM_DRIVER MESA_D3D12_DEFAULT_ADAPTER_NAME

pkill -9 -f "turtlebot4_gz_bringup" 2>/dev/null
pkill -9 -f "ros_gz_bridge"          2>/dev/null
pkill -9 -f "gz sim"                 2>/dev/null
sleep 2
rm -f /dev/shm/fastrtps_* /dev/shm/sem.fastrtps_* /dev/shm/*fastdds* 2>/dev/null

echo "[sim_start_headless] launching HEADLESS TB4 (world=$WORLD, namespace=robot_1) ..."
exec ros2 launch ~/robotics/sim_headless.launch.py \
  namespace:=robot_1 rviz:=false world:="$WORLD"
